gallery.title: File:Dinghuis.jpg
gallery.credit: Given to me by the author for putting it on commons
gallery.description: The 'Dinghuis' in Maastricht, The Netherlands. The building has been used for political and juridical purposes, and later used to be a theater. Currently, the bottom floor contains the Tourist Information Office. The name is derived from the Dutch word 'geding', which means 'lawsuit' and stems from the original use as a courtroom. So not to be confused with the Dutch word 'ding', which means 'thing', a common misconception.

gallery.title: File:Maastricht University - Campus Randwyck.jpg
gallery.description: Maastricht, the Netherlands. View of Randwyck, the business and university district in the southeast of Maastricht. To the left the University Hospital. To the right the School for Midwifery (Academie Verloskunde), part of Zuyd University of Applied Sciences. Untill 2013 the building also housed BioPartner (or Brains Unlimited), part of the Maastricht Health Campus. In 2013 Brains Unlimited moved to a new building in Oxfordlaan.)

gallery.title: File:Maastricht2013, CharlesEyckpark08.jpg
gallery.description: Maastricht, the Netherlands. View towards the South of Charles Eyckpark and Maaspuntweg along the Meuse river in the Céramique neighbourhood. The park was created in 1999-2000 after a design by Swedish landscape architect Gunnar Martinson and is named after the dutch painter and sculptor Charles Eyck. To the left: the Stoa building (designed by Luigi Snozzi). Far end of the road: Bonnefantenmuseum (designed by Aldo Rossi). Far right: Kennedy Bridge.
